rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal multiprofile modeling. This configuration tests standard encoders (scgpt + resnet50) with simple aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (concat), isolating the core multimodal interaction. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines and identifies if basic fusion methods suffice, providing foundational insights before exploring more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt+resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves 51.2% accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other components identical) improves performance. It isolates the impact of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, with minimal changes. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses uncertainty about fusion effectiveness without altering multiple parameters.

Existing evidence shows weighted fusion (config_004) outperforms concat (config_001). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation while retaining weighted fusion, scgpt/rn50 encoders, and multiprofile setting. It isolates the impact of aggregation method on performance, a critical design choice with uncertain optimal value.

Existing evidence shows weighted fusion (config_004) outperforms concat (config_001) in multimodal multiprofile setups. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping scgpt RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It isolates the impact of image encoder architecture, which is critical for multimodal performance, without changing other factors.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_031) outperforms resnet50 (config_004). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from scgpt (used in config_031) to scvi_n200 while keeping the image encoder, aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted) the same would improve performance. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice with the already validated image encoder, helping resolve uncertainty about which RNA representation is better under the optimal image encoder.

Existing evidence shows that config_007 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with avgpool and weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer and fusion from weighted to concat (while keeping the high-performing encoders) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation and fusion methods, which are critical design choices, and builds on the strong foundation of config_007 without overcomplicating other factors.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_046) achieves high accuracy (0.720). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder and weighted fusion (while keeping imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation) could further improve performance. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice and fusion method, which are critical design decisions with sparse evidence in previous experiments.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (config_046) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the profile setting to singleprofile (while adjusting aggregation and fusion) affects performance, isolating the impact of profile setting. It builds on the top-performing configuration by exploring a critical design choice with minimal risk, balancing exploitation of strong evidence and exploration of profile settings.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion achieves high accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion (while keeping scvi_n200 RNA and transformer aggregation) improves performance, isolating the impact of image encoder and fusion method. It balances exploration of critical design choices without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_046) can achieve high accuracy, but the impact of RNA/image encoder choices (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) remains uncertain. This experiment tests the effect of switching to pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders while retaining transformer aggregation and concat fusion (used in top-performing configs). It isolates the encoder impact, helping determine if these choices are critical for performance.
